description: General rules on ritningar och beskrivningar (drawings and specifications) and their precedence, plus CAD/BIM digital information handling.

entries.title_en: What the technical execution rests on
entries.text_en: Ritningar and beskrivningar are the basis for the technical execution of most larger construction projects. Ritningar are built on standards and standardised drawing symbols. Tekniska beskrivningar most often link to AMA.

entries.title_en: What a complete set of bygghandlingar usually contains
Drawings and specifications complement each other
entries.text_en: In contracts it normally applies that ritningar and beskrivningar complement each other. The prescribed execution does not need to be described in both the ritning and the beskrivning. It is therefore important that the fitter (montören) on site always has access to the beskrivning.
In the event of a conflict between ritning and beskrivning, the beskrivning takes precedence over the ritning (in an utförandeentreprenad, i.e. a design-bid-build contract).
entries.takeoff_implication: When automated reading of a ritning conflicts with the beskrivning, the beskrivning wins. Flag the conflict rather than silently trusting the drawing.

entries.text_en: In addition to the text in the beskrivning, the text in AMA applies. Because a code and its associated heading from AMA appear in the beskrivning, both the text under that heading in AMA and the text in superordinate headings are invoked, according to the so-called pyramidregeln (pyramid rule). If there is a conflict between AMA's text and the text of the beskrivning, the beskrivning applies.

entries.title_en: Other documents that apply on site
entries.text_en: There are several other documents to take into account on the construction site, for example environmental and work-environment rules and the manufacturers' installation instructions (monteringsanvisningar).
An important task on site is to continuously enter changes made during construction on a separate set of drawings, as the basis for relationsritningar.

Ritningar and beskrivningar can be produced according to Bygghandlingar 90. A standard for drawing symbols on VVS-ritningar is SIS 32260, which differs somewhat from the European standard. The industry also has praxis that can differ considerably from case to case, depending on the consultants' and clients' own routines.

paragraphs_en: BIM, Byggnads Informations Modellering (Building Information Modelling), is systematic digital information handling in construction projects. Designers draw the building and its installations in 3D models. These contain objects with properties. For a pump, for example, there is data on weight, dimensions, pump curve, electrical data, installation instructions, operation and maintenance instructions and byggvarudeklaration (construction product declaration). The information is accessible to everyone concerned.

In the design stage you can walk around the model - as in a computer game or with VR technology - and check buildability and coordination between the different technical disciplines. Dimensioning, for example pressure drop calculation for the heating system, can be carried out.

From the 3D models information can be exported to systems for kalkyl (estimating), setting out, planning, purchasing, logistics, facility management, operation and maintenance. Drawings, dimensions and other data are easily produced from the model. Extracts to tablets make the work easier for the fitter, the inspector and operating staff.

In many projects the model is used today together with 'produktionsprogram' instead of drawings as an aid for fitters in their work. There they can view the model in both 2D and 3D, measure, carry out self-checks, report deviations and so on. This gives better documentation, higher quality and often faster handling of questions.

BIP, Building Information Properties, and the classification system CoClass, with systematic designations and properties, make it possible for the information to be reused in several steps. BIP QTO makes it possible to obtain quantities sorted and summed for other systems.

In the facility management stage, operating staff can extract information from the model, for example a spare parts list for repair or replacement. The model can be used on tablets as support in work orders and when reporting back on measures taken. Ahead of a rebuild, all information about the existing installations is available.
All of this requires that the information is entered at the manufacturer stage, during design and in the relationshandlingar.
